questions.question: Which river basin covers an area of 65,145 km², of which about 80% liesin Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Tapi Basin.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Tapi Basin is situated in the northern part of the Deccan Plateau and extends over an area of 65145 sqkm which is nearly 2% of the total geographical area of the country.
 
• Nearly 80% of the basin lies in the State of Maharashtra.
 
• It lies between 72°33’ to 78°17’ east longitudes and 20°9’ to 21°50’ north latitudes. 
 
• The basin is bounded by the Satpura range on the north, by the Mahadev hills on the east, by the Ajanta Range and the Satmala hills on the south and by the Arabian Sea on the west.
 
• The Tapi is the second largest westward draining river of the Peninsula.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Godavari basin**. The Godavari River basin is the longest river in Maharashtra and the second-longest river in India after Ganga. 
 
• The total length of the river is 1,465 km.
 
• Godavari river rises near Nasik in Maharashtra at an elevation of about 1067 m and flows for a length of about **1465 km** before outfalling into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• 
 
 
 **The Godavari** originates in the Western Ghats of central India near Nashik in Maharashtra, from the Arabian Sea.

questions.question: Delhi ridge is the water divide between which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganges and Indus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Delhi Ridge is a northern extension of the ancient Aravalli Range.
 
• The ridge acts as a natural barrier and water divide between the Ganges and Indus river systems.
 
• It extends from the southeastern parts of Haryana through Delhi to the Yamuna river.
 
• The ridge plays a crucial role in the local climate, biodiversity, and water management of the Delhi region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Divide**

 
 
• A water divide, also known as a watershed or drainage divide, is a geographical boundary that separates neighboring drainage basins.
 
• Water divides determine the direction in which water flows and are crucial for managing water resources and preventing floods.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Range**
 
 
• The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, dating back to the Proterozoic era.
 
• It runs approximately 692 km across northwestern India, from Delhi to Gujarat.
 
• The range plays a vital role in influencing the climate and hydrology of the region.
 
 
 
• **Ganges River**
 
 
• The Ganges, also known as Ganga, is a major river in the Indian subcontinent, flowing through India and Bangladesh.
 
• It is considered sacred in Hinduism and is vital for agriculture, industry, and domestic use.
 
 
 
• **Indus River**
 
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, flowing through China (Tibet), India, and Pakistan.
 
• It is a key water source for agriculture and is historically significant as the cradle of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.

questions.question: The Ganga plain extend between which two rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghaggar and Teesta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ganga Plain which lies between **Ghaggar and Teesta** rivers is characterized by quaternary alluvia with combinations of clay, silt, sand, and gravel.
 
• The states,** of Haryana, Delhi, UP, Bihar, part of Jharkhand, and West Bengal** lie in the Ganga plains.
 
• This plain covers most of the part of Northern Plains.
 
• The Ganga plain stretches from** Delhi to Kolkata** covering about** 3.7 lakh sq km**.
 
• The peninsular rivers like** Ken, Chambal, Betwa, Son,** etc. joining the Ganga river system contributed to the formation of this plain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India is divided into six main parts that are The Great Mountain Range, Northern Plains, Desert Region, Peninsular Plateaus, Coastal Plains, and Island group. 
 
• The total geographical area of India is** 3.28 million square km**.
 
• The longest river in India is** Ganga** which is** 2,525 km** long.
 
• India has the** 18th largest Exclusive Economic Zone** of** 2,305,143 km2 (890,021 sq mi)**.
 
• India has **7,516 km** long coastline. Canada has the longest coastline in the world.

questions.question: Through which of the following states does the Rushikulya river pass?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Rushikulya River** is one of the **major rivers **in the state of **Odisha**.

 
 
• It covers the entire catchment area in the **districts **of **Kandhamal **and **Ganjam district **of Odisha.
 
• The **Rushikulya originates **at an **elevation **of about **1000 metres** from the **Daringbadi hills **of the **Eastern Ghats **range.
 
• The place from where the river **originates**, **Daringbadi **is called the ‘ **Kashmir of Odisha**.‘
 
• It **meets **the** Bay of Bengal** at **Puruna Bandha **in **Ganjam**.
 
• Its **tributaries **are the **Bagua**, the **Dhanei**, the **Badanadi **etc.
 
• It has** no delta **as such at its mouth.

questions.question: Which among the following is Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kanwar lake** is the largest oxbow lake in **India and in Asia**.
 
• It is a **freshwater lake** located in the** Begusarai district** and is the **only Ramsar site in Bihar**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wular Lake** is the **largest freshwater lake** in **India**, located in the state of **Jammu and Kashmir**.

 
 
• While it is a significant lake in terms of **size,** it is not classified as an **oxbow lake.**
 
• **Wular Lake** is a result of** tectonic activity** and is fed by the J**helum River.**
 
 
 
• **Bhojtal, **also known as **Upper Lake,** is a** large lake** located in **Bhopal**, the capital city of the state of** Madhya Pradesh** in **India**.
 
 
• It is an artificial lake created by Raja Bhoj during his reign. 
 
 
 
• **Nakki Lake **is a popular tourist attraction located in Mount Abu, a hill station in the state of **Rajasthan, India.**
 
• It is a small and **scenic lake surrounded by hills**.

questions.question: With reference to the major regions of the northern plains, Bhabar is:

options.text: the older alluvium along the river beds forming terraces higher than the flood plain
a narrow belt of about 8 to 16 km that runs in the west-east direction along the foot of the Himalayas from the river Indus to Teesta
composed of newer alluvium and forms flood plains along the river banks
a broad long zone of northern India and southern Nepal running parallel to the lower ranges of the Himalayas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **After going down **from the **mountain **a **narrow belt **is formed which **is 8-16 km by the deposition **of **river pebbles**. This **belt **is called **Bhabar**. 
 
• It lies **parallel **to the **Shiwalik range**. **Streams again appear **in this **region **and **make it a wet **and **marshy region**.
 
• **The bhabar **tract comprises gravel and **un-assorted sediment deposits**.
 
• **This sediment present **in the **soil **is **deposited **by **rivers descending **from the **Himalayan mountains**.
 
• **This region **is not **good for cultivation**. **The area **is popular **with big trees with large roots**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhangar** - is the older alluvium along the river beds forming terraces, which are dark in colour, rich in humus content and productive. Bhangar is generally a well-drained and the most productive land of the Great Plains of India.
 
• **The Khadar** is composed of newer alluvium and forms the flood plains along the river banks. They are sandy clays and loams, drier and leached, less calcareous and carbonaceous.
 
• **Tarai,** also spelled Terai, region of northern India and southern Nepal running parallel to the lower ranges of the Himalayas.
